agent_notes: Reviewed the full settings.html plus the save_settings handler (triggarr/web/routes.py:519-541) for injection, XSS, secrets, auth, and mass-assignment impact. All interpolated values (log_level, hard_max_per_cycle, inst_name, app_name, etc.) continue to go through Jinja2's default autoescaping with no `| safe` added or autoescape disabled anywhere in this diff; no new user input is rendered unescaped.

No CSRF token input exists in any of the three <form> elements (General, Security, per-app instances) before or after this diff, consistent with the project's middleware-based CSRF enforcement (tests/test_middleware.py) rather than a per-form token -- splitting the General section into its own <form> does not remove or weaken a per-form CSRF control that existed before.

Not a security finding, but worth flagging for the bugs/correctness reviewer: the new General <form> (lines 18-90) has no submit button and is never POSTed. The only 'Save Settings' button lives in the separate per-app instances <form> (lines 134-246), whose handler (triggarr/web/routes.py:531-539) treats absent fields as 'use default', not 'preserve existing' -- e.g. `safe_log_level(form.get('log_level'))` and `form.get('skip_unreleased') == 'on'`. Because General's fields are outside that form, every click of 'Save Settings' (e.g. adding/editing an app instance) will silently reset log_level, hard_max_per_cycle, max_history_rows, request_timeout, page_size, tracking_window_minutes, max_consecutive_failures, and skip_unreleased back to hardcoded defaults, overwriting the user's configured values. This looks like a data-integrity/availability regression, not an attacker-exploitable vulnerability in the categories I check, so I'm surfacing it here rather than as a finding.
